children: Mesabi Trust reported second-quarter fiscal 2026 results, delivering $2.33M of revenue for the three months ended July 31, 2026, and a net loss of $95K, or $(0.0072) per unit, as royalty income declined sharply versus the year‑ago period.
Revenue was $2.33M for Q2 fiscal 2026 (three months ended July 31, 2026), down from $5.42M in the year‑ago quarter (57.0% decline).
Net income was a loss of $95.0K in Q2 fiscal 2026, versus net income of $4.74M in the year‑ago quarter.
Diluted earnings per unit was $(0.0072) for Q2 fiscal 2026, down from $0.3616 per unit in the year‑ago quarter.
Royalty income fell materially year-to-date as pellet prices declined, eliminating bonus royalties and reducing cash available for distributions.
Pellet production and shipments increased versus the prior year (1.88M tons YTD), with 100% of production originating from Trust lands.
Cliffs shifted more sales to internal affiliates, reducing arms‑length third‑party sales and creating uncertainty in royalty calculations.
Northshore exited an extended maintenance shutdown that occurred in 2025, which boosted 2026 production; the Mesabi Metallics direct‑reduction project is progressing nearby.
Trustees reduced the unallocated reserve and cut the quarterly distribution to $0.05 per unit amid lower royalties and higher legal expenses.
